chapter: Philadelphia, Detroit and back to Atlantic City
title: Lucky Roberts and Eubie Blake's advice about hands
summary: Through Charley Johnson he meets Lucky Roberts, whose big hands and Junkman Rag amazed him, and Eubie Blake tells him not to throw his hands in the air.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: at that time had more instruments than the bands in the east. Because we was just beginning to take them on in the east. Because we had so much trouble with the -- oh, on account of the people in the summertime in Atlantic City, they stayed up and there was so many people. The cabarets were right in the neighborhood where some legitimate people lived, you see. And when they raised the windows in the summertime, and you could hear all kinds of noise. So, while I was in Atlantic City, I renewed my friendship with Charley Johnson again. And that's when he -- through Charley Johnson, I had a chance to meet men like Lucky Roberts. Lucky Roberts came down there with a show. And, well, that's one of the greatest guys that I've known to play a piano. What happened, Lucky had a great big hand, and he had two big hands, like some of these, Rachmaninoff, for instance. He has big hands like that. And he stretched the keys. And when he played, especially one piece called, "The Junkman Rag", it sounded like he was a whole band playing.

I don't remember much, but I remember he used to do something like this. (plays piano). Well, he used to do something like that. And then he had another thing he used to throw his hands in the air, you know, like this. And so, when he threw those hands in the air, I was trying to get that. I didn't have that at the time, because another friend

of mine discouraged me from doing that. And that was Eubie Blake. He said, "Kid, you can't play with your hands in the air. Keep them on the piano. You can hardly play with them on the piano, so what are you throwing your hands in the air for?" See, one reason I think Eubie was saying that, was sometimes, because I don't think he could do that.
